newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zairean rebels claim town in far northeast.
newsitem.headline: Zairean rebels claim town in far northeast.

text.p: Zairean rebel leader Laurent Kabila said on Thursday his forces were advancing on multiple fronts despite government warplanes dropping napalm and had seized the main town in the northeast corner of Zaire.
"Our forces captured Faradje late yesterday (Wednesday)," Kabila told reporters in this eastern town facing Burundi. "They have now cleared the way up to the Sudan border."
If true, the capture of Faradje would mean the rebels since October have captured a swath of eastern territory at least 1,095 km (675 miles) long bordering Uganda, Rwanda, Burundi and Tanzania.

Faradje is the most northeasterly town in Zaire but rebels had already taken Isiro, 260 km (160 miles) southwest. Kinshasa said fell Isiro fell to the rebels on Wednesday night, a day after rebels said they had seized it.

Faradje is 60 km (40 miles) from the border with Sudan but it was unclear if it would help the rebels obtain supplies since a civil war is raging in southern Sudan between Khartoum's forces and Sudanese rebels.

Kabila also said the town of Lubutu, southeast of the key centre of Kisangani, was besieged by rebels. He said the main government army brigade was pulled back to Kisangani, leaving only a small unit to stop the rebels.
He said government jets on Wednesday dropped napalm on rebel positions near Lubutu and one rebel had been burned. There was no independent confirmation of the napalm report.
In Kinshasa, a senior defence ministry official said on Thursday the army planned to reinforce Kisangani, the headquarters for its military operations in the war zone in the east.
"We are planning to send more fresh troops into Kisangani over the weekend. The situation necessitates reinforcements," added the official.
On the southernmost front, Kabila said his forces were still advancing on Moba, a port of Lake Tanganyika, following their capture of Kalemie in the mineral-rich province of Shaba.

Kabila's Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire (AFDL) has staged graduation parades for 6,700 newly-trained recruits in its three eastern centres of Uvira, Goma and Bukavu within the last week.
Uganda, Burundi and Rwanda have all denied accusations from Kinshasa that they had sent troops into eastern Zaire to fight alongside rebels.
In Lusaka, the U.N. refugee agency said at least 6,000 people fleeing Zaire's civil war were expected to arrive in neighbouring Zambia on barges across Lake Tanganyika later on Thursday.
UNHCR Protection Officer Ron Mponda told Reuters eight Zairean soldiers were among those fleeing Zaire and had laid down their weapons and would be granted refugee status.
